Programme start date: September 2027

Please review all the graduate programme opportunities and make one application

Our award-winning graduate programme provides the ideal springboard for an exciting and meaningful career in global financial markets.  LSEG is at the forefront of trading services – a fundamental part of the financial and transactional services that support and enhance the development of businesses and economies across the world.

Success graduates will join LSEG’s Markets division on the rotational programme
and be part of a dynamic team that powers global financial markets and helps organisations navigate risk with confidence. This graduate programme brings together our Capital Markets and Post Trade businesses to offer a comprehensive suite of solutions—from raising and trading capital across asset classes and geographies, to clearing and optimising portfolios, to managing regulatory, reputational and financial risk.

Whether it’s enabling companies to list and grow on the London Stock Exchange, supporting seamless post-trade operations, or delivering trusted data and tools like World-Check and identity verification services, you’ll be at the heart of the financial ecosystem. You’ll gain exposure to cutting-edge platforms like FXall and Tradeweb, work with clients across the globe, and help shape the future of financial markets.

This is a great opportunity for students studying a Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics subject
or Finance, Economics with a strong inclination towards FinTech/Technology to apply their skills to Business related role. During the recruitment process we will get to know your skills and interest and how they align with the needs of the business to place you in your first rotation.

As a graduate you can expect exposure across:

Financial Risk teams, which involves monitoring and analysing risks, and interpreting data in readiness for the delivery of risk projects or reporting.
Or supporting our existing products! Contributing towards researching, tracking, and testing content and user interface of online products.
Or research analysis into global markets which could have a focus on debt listings, valuations, and shareholder and geographic analysis.  

To be eligible you must be a graduate studying a Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics discipline, who has completed your studies in 2026 or a final year undergraduate or Master’s student and have completed all the requirements of your qualification before September 2027. 

Highlights of the Graduate Programme

Progress through a 12-month development journey aiming to build foundational skills that are key for your future success
Build your foundational knowledge of LSEG, Financial Markets and the business during your global induction
Divisional-led inductions to immerse graduates into the business through team-led overviews and introductions
Participate in group projects which are aligned to LSEG goals

Access opportunities to earn industry recognized qualifications, including 5 study days during programme
Connect with global early careers community and opportunities and contribute to wider society via CSR initiatives and volunteering opportunities 

Our graduates join us on a permanent basis, and from day one you will be aligned to LSEG Markets, which will allow you to develop within a secure framework.

We are passionate about recruiting people who want to understand the full breadth of our organisation, how it fits together, how it functions – and are interested in playing a part of our development, as it grows and diversifies. 

You should have a demonstrable interest in financial markets, which you’ve built through your studies, work experience or extracurricular activities. 
Competent and comfortable with large data sets and able to code in the relevant languages (Python, SQL) or an understanding of tools like Tableu, Power BI
A curiosity for data and an ability to analyse information to draw conclusions and propose solutions. 
Individuals who are able to connect the dots and think strategically.  
The environment we work in is fast paced, you’ll need to demonstrate focus, resilience and the flexibility to adapt to changing demands. 
People who can collaborate with others, using their strong communication skills in the process. 
Studying a Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics discipline or Finance, Economics with a strong inclination towards FinTech/Technology. 
Ideal candidates will have the rights to work in the UK without restrictions for the duration of the graduate programme and joins us on a permanent basis from day one.

You will stand out to us if you can demonstrate and recognise that what you achieve is equally important as how you achieve it. 

Application close: 20th October,
however we recommend an early application as we consider candidates on a rolling basis. Due to the volume of applications, we might close the applications earlier, so we recommend an early application.  

Recruitment Process:

The first stage of the recruitment process involves making an application and submitting your resume.
The next stage of the application process is an untimed Immersive Online Assessment. The assessment is designed to give you an insight into what it’s like to work at LSEG.
The second stage is a video interview where you will answer a series of questions using a strength-based-interview style
The final stage is a half day assessment centre which involves several different types of exercises – further information is provided at the point of invite. 

Please review all the graduate programme opportunities and make
one application If you make more than one application, we will review your first application only.

Active DoD Secret clearance or the ability to obtain one.

jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager, AMXL CX, AMXL CX & Growth
jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Extra Large (AMXL) is a single-threaded organization that owns the end-to-end customer experience for heavy and bulky products, from supply chain and fulfillment through transportation, last mile delivery, and post-purchase resolution. AMXL currently operates across North America, Europe, Japan, and is expanding into emerging markets. Within AMXL, the CX and Growth org is a centralized, worldwide team organized across five pillars designed to ensure that every customer who purchases a large, high-value product receives a reliable experience.

The Execution Excellence pillar is where planning meets the customer. It houses two complementary teams: our AMXL Operations Center and our AMXL Proactive Execution program. These teams serve as the real-time network execution backbone, translating strategic decisions into daily network performance across our end-to-end network and also as the mechanism that identifies delivery failures before they become visible to the customer and intervenes proactively to save the delivery or manage the recovery directly with the customer. Together, these teams form a closed loop: detect upstream, prevent where possible, intervene proactively where not, and feed root causes back so defects are resolved at the source.

We are seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead the integration and transformation of this combined organization. This is not a steady-state program management role. The program strategy is being built. You will inherit a consolidation in progress and own the lifecycle of making it work: assessing what the combined org should look like, defining how we measure success, building the mechanisms that make it sustainable, and driving the hard conversations required to get there. You will use process lifecycle evaluation methodologies to categorize the team's portfolio (automate, simplify, reallocate, or deprecate), and build automation roadmaps in partnership with technical teams.

This role requires someone who can operate in high ambiguity, make trade-offs between short-term operational needs and long-term strategic goals, and communicate persuasively across teams. The right candidate sees automation and AI as something they use today, not something they plan to use later, and will set the standard for how this team uses technology to scale impact without scaling headcount.

Key job responsibilities

Define the operating model for the combined organization: org design, process rationalization, scope definition, and mechanisms that make it self-sustaining.
Build the process lifecycle evaluation framework, determining which workflows to automate, simplify, reallocate, or retire, and manage the pipeline of new use cases from scoping through launch.
Own the automation roadmap in partnership with data science, engineering, and technology teams, establishing accountability mechanisms with clear timelines for every manual process.
Drive cross-functional stakeholder alignment across supply chain, quality, and operations, navigating complex organizational dynamics and building trust where needed.
Scale this capability into new geographies by adapting the operating model to local carrier ecosystems, regulatory environments, and workforce availability.

A day in the life

You might start your morning reviewing program metrics dashboards, identifying areas that need attention, and preparing a status narrative for a director-level review. By mid-morning you are facilitating a working session with partners to align on priorities for the quarter. After lunch you dive into data to validate assumptions behind a proposed solution, then draft a decision document that frames trade-offs for leadership. You close the day mentoring a newer program manager and connecting with cross-regional counterparts to keep workstreams on track.

About The Team

The AMXL Customer Experience and Growth team takes a 360-degree approach to the customer journey:

**Eliminate**: detect, solve, and resolve customer-impacting issues upstream by providing relevant and timely insights for operations teams, transportation, and product development.
**Automate**: continuously assess and identify opportunities to replace manual processes with automated, scalable solutions.
**Optimize**: when a customer does need support, ensure AMXL stakeholders have the tools, resources, policies, and protocols to deliver a perfect experience.

The operations center translates strategic decisions into daily network performance. The proactive execution team ensures that when defects occur, customers are protected through early intervention. The Sr. Program Manager will be the link that makes both teams operate as one system.

Basic Qualifications

Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience implementing repeatable processes and driving automation or standardization
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Knowledge of general AI tools
Experience defining and executing program requirements
Speak, write, and read fluently in English

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years of driving process improvements experience
Master's degree, or MBA in supply chain, business, engineering, finance or related technical or quantitative field
Experience managing programs across multiple countries and time zones

jobs.title: Business Continuity Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Daiwa Capital Markets America Inc.:

Incorporated in 1964, Daiwa Capital Markets America Inc. (“DCMA”) is a New York-based registered securities broker-dealer, a futures commission merchant, a primary dealer of U.S. Treasury securities, and a member of the New York Stock Exchange and other major U.S. exchanges. Our main focus is on the sales and trading of Japanese, Asian, and U.S. equities, fixed income instruments, financial futures, and investment banking for institutional customers. DCMA’s ultimate parent company is Daiwa Securities Group Inc., one of the largest brokerage and financial services groups in Japan.

Position Summary:

We are seeking a Business Continuity Program Manager who will be responsible for ensuring that our organization has effective business continuity plans in place that can withstand potential disruptions. In this role, you will be responsible for maintaining and refreshing all BCP policies, standards, and documentation, coordinating disaster recovery testing, and working with compliance and legal departments to ensure plans meet regulatory and industry standards. Reporting to the Head of Information Technology, this business-critical role will lead and oversee the Firm’s BCP program.

Core Responsibilities:

Lead and oversee the Firm’s Business Continuity Program, including the ongoing maintenance, governance, and enhancement of BCP policies, standards, playbooks, plans, and related documentation.
Partner with departmental leaders and business continuity coordinators to ensure firmwide and department-specific BCP documentation, testing processes, and recovery procedures remain current and aligned with business needs.
Maintain the Firm’s Operational Resilience framework by conducting annual Business Impact Analyses, validating RPOs/RTOs, assessing critical business processes and applications, and identifying areas of vulnerability.
Coordinate firmwide disaster recovery testing, including business-critical application testing, file restore testing, SIFMA industry-wide DR testing, and RegSCI testing, including after-hours and weekend support as required.
Serve as a key member of the Firm’s Emergency and Crisis Management Teams, Pandemic Planning Committee, and Cyber Response Teams, supporting coordinated response planning across business and control functions.
Provide 24x7 support during events requiring activation of all or part of the Firm’s business continuity plans, acting as a primary point of contact for senior management and facilitating cross-functional response efforts.
Partner with Risk Management, Internal Audit, Information Security, Legal, Compliance, and Third-Party Risk Management to ensure business continuity plans meet regulatory, audit, industry, and vendor readiness requirements.
Manage business continuity reviews conducted by Internal Audit, external auditors, and Compliance, ensuring findings, comments, and remediation items are addressed in a timely and effective manner.
Lead quarterly governance meetings with departmental coordinators and executive management to report on testing progress, escalate issues, and drive accountability for remediation and program improvements.
Manage and maintain the Firm’s business continuity site in Iselin, NJ, ensuring readiness to support business operations during disruption events.
Advance the maturity of the Business Continuity Program by identifying opportunities to strengthen resilience, enhance recovery capabilities, and automate manual processes.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Business Administration, or related field
7+ years of experience in Business Continuity Planning, Disaster Recovery, and the design and maintenance of an enterprise-wide Business Impact Analysis.
In-depth knowledge of regulatory requirements and guidance, e.g., RegSCI / SIFMA Classic, etc.
Familiarity with SQL databases / queries and reporting services like Crystal Reports and PowerBI.
Must have the ability to travel to Iselin, NJ every 2 weeks.
Ability to work weekends and after hours to coordinate off-hours BCP tests with various vendors, and regulatory bodies (SIFMA, FIA, etc.).
Strong project management, leadership, and customer service skills.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work independently under tight deadlines and minimal guidance.
Availability to provide 24x7 support during emergencies and significant disruption events.

Work Arrangements & Availability:

This position operates in a hybrid work environment and requires onsite presence at our midtown Manhattan office a minimum of three days per week, and your ability to visit our BCP site in Iselin, New Jersey at least once every 2 weeks.
Your hybrid / in-office days are determined by management based on business and operational requirements.
You must be able to provide onsite support during business-critical incidents, technology outages, audits, and operational events including early morning coverage beginning as early as 7:00 AM when required.

Company Culture and Benefits:

Daiwa Capital Markets America Inc. has a vibrant company culture made up of a diverse team of professionals. We seek to foster an atmosphere in which our employees understand, respect, and inspire each other. We will continue to build a culture that encourages everyone at DCMA to take pride in their work. How we work — individually, with each other, and with our communities — is just as important as what we do and shapes who we are as an organization.

Kestra Financial, a leading provider of wealth management platforms, technology solutions, and investment products empowering independent financial advisors and RIAs nationwide, is seeking a Senior Strategic Implementation Manager.

This role serves as a pivotal execution leader accountable for the disciplined delivery of Kestra Wealth Management’s highest-priority strategic initiatives in investment products and platform capabilities. Map and manage complex dependencies, risks, and interdependencies across teams; proactively identify and remove blockers while fostering alignment and shared ownership in a matrixed environment.
Ensure every initiative incorporates appropriate compliance guardrails, risk controls, audit readiness, and change management from the start.
Design, implement, and continuously mature agile delivery operating models tailored to regulated investment product and platform initiatives. This includes establishing Scrum-like cadences (sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, retrospectives), Kanban for workflow transparency and flow optimization, and scaled frameworks (e.g., program-level planning or release management) for larger or interdependent efforts.
Stand up consistent governance rhythms and forums, including steering committees, launch readiness reviews/tollgates, dependency management sessions, risk reviews, and clear escalation paths to executive leadership.
Drive adoption of modern agile/project tools (Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or equivalent) and best practices to improve delivery velocity, predictability, collaboration, and quality across technology and business teams.
Champion a shift toward iterative, outcome-focused delivery—balancing the need for structure and compliance in product launches with the speed and adaptability required in a competitive wealth tech landscape.
Build and operate a portfolio “control tower” capability: deliver timely, credible, decision-oriented reporting and dashboards on initiative status, milestones, risks/issues, dependencies, financial performance (budget vs. plan, ROI tracking), and leading indicators of business impact.
Define, track, and report on key business outcome metrics tied to each strategic initiative (e.g., new product net flows/AUM/revenue contribution, advisor adoption and usage rates, client/advisor satisfaction or NPS impact, reduction in time-to-market or launch cycle time, compliance adherence, platform feature utilization and engagement).
Proactively surface execution risks, capacity constraints, and recommended trade-offs to senior leadership; lead structured issue resolution, corrective action planning, and recovery efforts to protect delivery commitments and protect/enhance business results.
Prepare and present high-quality materials for executive leadership, steering committees, and governance forums; represent the delivery health and outlook of the Investment Platforms & Products portfolio with clarity and fact-based insights.
Instill a culture of genuine accountability—where teams own and are measured on the delivery of agreed business outcomes and value realization, not merely activity completion or milestone hitting.

What You Bring:

2+ years experience in technical product management in an Agile environment.
5+ years of experience in wealth management, investment operations, or trading
3-5+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic program/portfolio management, product implementation, launch execution, or enterprise transformation roles within wealth management, RIA platforms, investment product development, fintech, asset/wealth platforms, or similarly complex, regulated financial services environments.

We value ownership, execution, growth, intelligence, and camaraderie. We are looking for people who share our core values, thrive, and contribute to this environment while putting the customer first. We are seeking a Service Operations Analyst (Pod) to join our growing Service Operations team within a Managed Services Provider (MSP) environment.

This role is designed for a senior individual contributor who can bring structure, follow-through, and operational ownership across one or more service delivery pods.

The Service Operations Analyst (Pod) acts as the connective layer across Clients, Service Delivery, Support Managers, Project Managers, Support Managers, and Finance to ensure key workflows move forward consistently, risks are surfaced early, and nothing critical gets stuck.

This is not a traditional administrative support role. It is a higher-ownership position focused on operational excellence, cross-functional coordination, workflow maturity, and helping shape how the pod support model evolves as Atlas continues to scale.

Pod Operational Ownership:

Act as the Service Operations point person for one or more service delivery pods.
Bring visibility to open actions, blockers, service risks, and operational dependencies across teams.
Reduce dependencies on Support Managers for non-technical work.
Ensure work moves forward consistently through structured follow-up, accountability, and clear ownership.

Client Health, QBR Readiness, And Service Visibility

Drive QBR readiness and post-QBR follow-through across assigned scope.
Monitor client health indicators, including backlog trends, SLA risks, service escalations, CSAT/NPS inputs, and other operational signals.
Help prepare pod-level visibility into performance, risks, and opportunities.
Ensure action items, opportunities, and service concerns identified through QBRs or leadership reviews are tracked to completion.

Partner with Support Managers, Project Managers to ensure internal execution and client expectations stay aligned.
Surface risks, delays, or coordination gaps early so they can be addressed before they affect the client experience.

Billing, Quote, And Commercial Workflow Ownership

Own and evolve billing-related workflows tied to support projects, recurring reviews, and monthly follow-through.
Monitor billing alignment, usage trends, exceptions, and revenue-impacting gaps.
Own quote management visibility and ensure proposals, pricing-related follow-through, and related approvals move efficiently.
Build regular checks and balances so Admin and Associate execution remains accurate, timely, and measurable.
Identify recurring breakdowns in workflow and propose more scalable operating structures.

Workflow Governance And Process Improvement

Own complex, cross-functional operational workflows end to end, ensuring they are clear, documented, and sustainable.
Simplify recurring work by improving process design rather than relying only on manual pushing and reminders.
Identify operational inefficiencies, recurring blockers, and unclear handoffs, then recommend practical improvements.
Help define standards, expectations, and service levels for key Service Ops workflows.

Tooling, Dashboards, And Operational Monitoring

Automation And Scale

Identify manual, repetitive work that can be simplified, automated, or shifted downward appropriately.
Reduce dependencies on Support Manager for non-technical work
Help define and support AI, automation, or workflow-improvement opportunities within Service Ops.
Measure whether changes are actually reducing manual load and improving consistency for Admin and Associate roles.

Qualifications

3+ years of experience in service operations, business operations, project coordination, or a related operational role, ideally within an MSP, IT services, or professional services environment.
Strong follow-through, ownership, and accountability.
Ability to manage multiple cross-functional priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong judgment in ambiguous situations, including knowing when to escalate and when to drive resolution directly.
Experience working with operational tools such as Monday.com, ConnectWise Manage, Power BI, Excel, or similar systems.
Comfort working across technical and non-technical teams.
Ability to create structure, improve workflows, and keep work moving without relying solely on management escalation.
Strong attention to detail and operational discipline.
Willingness to operate as a senior individual contributor in a role that is still evolving.

Desirable Qualities

Experience in an MSP, IT services, or professional services environment.
Experience supporting QBRs, client health reporting, or service delivery visibility.
Exposure to billing workflows, quote/proposal management, utilization tracking, or financial process coordination.
Ability to identify patterns, turn ambiguity into structure, and improve operating processes.

jobs.title: Lead Data Analyst, Growth & Experimentation
jobs.description:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care into the one-stop shop for all home services. Getting there depends on how fast we can test, learn, and scale what works.

About The Data Team

We're a high-leverage team of Product Data Analysts embedded across the business, owning the semantic layer and the metrics everyone trusts. The experimentation program runs on real rigor, not vibes: pre-registered analysis plans gate every test launch, anytime-valid statistics keep mid-run dashboards honest under continuous viewing, automated daily SRM and attribution health sweeps catch broken tests early, and seasonal power forecasting accounts for a business that swings hard by time of year. The test lifecycle, design through readout, is already AI-driven. Our analysts are stretched across product, so Growth support has stayed part-time and reactive, until now.

The Role

You're the first data analyst dedicated entirely to Growth and Experimentation. Your primary charter is the experimentation program
: test design, statistical rigor, and readouts across web funnels, SMS/drip, sales-driven tests, and SEO tests built on our own page-clustering tooling. It's a wider surface than most companies run. You also own the acquisition-to-conversion funnel
those tests move, across paid, organic, and partner channels. What to test and which direction to bet on is the CRO's and Growth PMs' call; you shape it, they decide it.

You're not starting from scratch. Dashboards, tooling, and rigor scaffolding are already shipped and running. Expect the early months to be hands-on and manual: scoping tests, crunching readouts, while you build toward a self-serve layer. If a test readout and a funnel refresh ever compete for your week, the test wins.

What Makes This Role Different

The CEO personally engages with test design here: real organizational weight, no fight for buy-in
You partner directly with the Director of CRO, performance marketing, and Growth PMs, who come to you when a test needs a call

Requirements

What You'll Own

Experimentation rigor: test design, power and sample-size calls, significance and readout standards. Core of the role: you catch underpowered tests and false positives before they become bad decisions, and you get Growth's tests onto the anytime-valid monitoring the program already runs, so early calls come from a crossed boundary instead of a hopeful trend read
The self-serve experimentation layer: automated Growth metrics in Lightdash, Python-backed stat-sig tooling, and the AI skills (Claude routines) already handling pre-test power calcs and live-test health checks. You extend these and keep the layer correct as product and tracking evolve
The Growth funnel model: a trusted, instrumented view of visitor → lead → customer across every brand and channel, with the CAC, LTV, and conversion-rate cuts Growth needs to prioritize investment
The Growth analytics function model: by end of Year 1, the standards and playbook that scale this function beyond one person, plus a buy-vs-build recommendation for the experimentation stack (an off-the-shelf stats engine, or extending our own skills and Python). You bring the recommendation; the final call isn't yours alone

Problems to Solve

Tests that can't answer the question they were run for
Growth wants more experiments, but volume without rigor produces confident, wrong conclusions. Raising the bar without becoming the bottleneck is the job.

Getting off the manual treadmill
Real tooling already exists: test-design helpers, dashboards, AI skills. Most tests are still hands-on and bespoke. How do you extend that automation so routine cases genuinely self-serve?

Making the funnel decision-grade
The semantic layer defines the funnel, but instrumentation is uneven across brands and channels, and no one owns the single trusted view. You build it, and you keep it trusted.

Turning analysis into decisions
The hard part isn't the SQL. It's getting a PM or marketer to change course. Can you deliver insight sharp enough that the room acts, and push back when the data favors the popular but wrong idea?

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

Rigor is the default. Power calculations are standard practice, early stops on Growth tests come from the anytime-valid boundary rather than a trend read, and the re-run rate (redone for tracking or attribution problems) is down
Routine tests self-serve. Metrics and stat-sig are automated in Lightdash, so the team reads standard results without filing a ticket, and your time goes to the tests that need an analyst
A funnel Growth trusts. The acquisition→conversion funnel is instrumented across every brand and channel; Growth prioritizes off your model, not side spreadsheets
Measurable conversion wins. Your analysis directly drove specific, quantified lifts in the funnel, and you can name them

Who You Are

AI-native.
You use AI daily for SQL, dbt, and pressure-testing your analysis, extending the skills already running our experimentation process rather than merely using them. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI or treat your workflow as fixed.

A partner, not a report-writer.
You don't wait for a ticket. You sit close to Growth and bring the question before anyone asks it. Skip this one if you want a clear queue with no expectation to push back.

Statistically sharp.
Wrong fit if "we hit significance" ends your analysis instead of starting it. Right fit if you have a point of view on test design (power, significance, novelty and interaction effects, when not to test) and can explain a broken experiment in plain terms.

Fluent in experiment instrumentation.
You know how Segment events and Flagsmith randomization interact, and catch a tracking problem before a test ships, keeping our re-run rate down. This isn't for you if instrumentation is someone else's job.

Fluent in the funnel.
You think in CAC, LTV, and channel economics, and know acquisition data's quirks: attribution messiness, seasonality, channel mix. Skip this one if your background is pure product-feature analytics.

Technically self-sufficient.
Wrong fit if you need clean data handed to you. Expert SQL, enough Python to automate the stat-sig math, and comfort in dbt and Lightdash, building your own models without waiting on data engineering.

Influences without authority.
PMs and marketers act on what you find because your insight is clear and honest about uncertainty. This isn't for you if you consider the job done once the analysis ships, regardless of outcome.

This Role Is NOT

A ticket queue. Not the role if you want well-defined asks: no one hands you a backlog of number-pulls, you decide what's worth measuring
The person who decides what to test. You shape that call and own its rigor, but the roadmap and final direction belong to the CRO and Growth PMs
A product-feature analyst seat. Existing analysts already own product, pricing, and service delivery; this one lives in Growth: acquisition, conversion, experimentation
A pure platform or dashboard-builder. You'll automate metrics, stat-sig, and AI skills into a self-serve layer, but that's the means. The job is designing experiments and keeping that automation correct as product and tracking evolve
A people-management role. This is an individual-contributor seat

Benefits

Base salary: $75,000-$100,000 USD annually
The scope is the draw: First analyst dedicated entirely to Growth and Experimentation, with your fingerprints on how this company decides what works
AI tooling provided: The Claude routines already running pieces of our experimentation process are yours to extend, not a side project you have to justify
Fully remote: This is deep-focus analytical work with US-facing partners. We hire the best analyst regardless of city and trust you to manage your environment and overlap hours
Flexible PTO: Measured on outcomes, not hours logged

Improved member retention
New member acquisition
Higher net interest margin
Improved rate competitiveness
Greater market share in expanded markets

Origination and core systems capable of supporting regional and channel-based pricing

New deposit products
Governance and compliance approvals
Frontline training
Website capability to display region-specific pricing

Lead the project through discovery, design, and execution, developing and managing an integrated project plan, budget, schedule, and scope across all workstreams.

Our Program Manager's are always thinking about the bigger picture. Every position at Amazon offers the opportunity for employees to influence business decisions and shape the future. Collaborating with a wide range of stakeholders across the business, you’ll continuously be scoping out new solutions. You’ll conduct your own research and analysis, always with an eye on the long-term vision of the business. This is your opportunity to have a big impact on some of the most exciting new ideas that are shaping the future of Amazon.

Create innovative solutions using data and research to address wider challenges in your organization
Take a big-picture approach in your analysis of business operations, driving improvements across a range of teams and organizations
Work alongside senior leadership to establish and prioritize improvement programs, seeing them through from start to finish
Enhance operational performance on every program in partnership with your stakeholders

As a Program Manager, you’ll drive and manage the implementation of creative, data-driven change in Amazon, leading improvement projects and programs. You’ll use strategic thinking to define and implement an efficient project plan. Some managers are based on-site while others work remotely, depending on the most suitable option for their team and tasks.

Program Managers have significant responsibilities, and you’ll deal with complex challenges with creativity, innovation, and leadership. When you click on your screen, and know that your Amazon parcel will arrive with you on the next day, you’ve just use one of the world’s most sophisticated fulfillment networks. new_jobs.description:
S.J. Louis Construction, Inc. | Nationwide (Hybrid) | Full-Time

Position Overview

S.J. Louis Construction is hiring a Senior Project Manager to lead complex heavy civil and underground infrastructure projects from preconstruction through closeout. This is a senior role with full accountability for project outcomes across safety, schedule, budget, quality, and client relationships on projects including large-diameter pipeline installations, pump stations, deep utility systems, and heavy civil work.

This is a hybrid position with time split between the office, home, and project sites. S.J. Louis covers all project-related travel expenses and pays a daily per diem for overnight assignments.

Key Responsibilities

Project Execution

Manage all project phases from planning and procurement through construction, startup, and closeout
Set up project team structure, communication schedules, and decision-making processes
Coordinate subcontractors, engineers, inspectors, vendors, and municipal stakeholders
Lead owner-architect-contractor meetings and serve as the main point of contact for clients
Mentor and develop Project Engineers and Project Managers on the team

Financial Management

Manage project budget, cost forecasting, and margin performance
Lead subcontractor buyout and handle contract administration
Process and negotiate change orders from identification through documentation and approval
Approve invoices and keep job cost reporting accurate and current

Schedule and Technical Oversight

Build and manage CPM schedules, milestone plans, and rolling look-aheads
Coordinate long-lead procurement to protect the schedule
Review and interpret civil, structural, mechanical, and utility drawings
Oversee construction sequencing for critical tie-ins, shutdowns, and bypass operations
Identify and work through field conflicts and constructability issues early

Safety and Quality

Enforce OSHA standards, company safety policies, and applicable municipal utility requirements
Set quality expectations at project start and verify work through inspections and documentation
Maintain complete project records that support decision-making and protect against claims

Required Experience

10 to 15 years of construction project management experience in heavy civil or underground utility work
At least 7 years managing projects involving underground utilities, large-diameter pipelines, pump stations, or heavy civil infrastructure
Experience managing projects valued at $10M to $50M or more
Strong working knowledge of gravity sewer, force mains, water mains, large-diameter pipelines (48-inch and larger), deep excavation, shoring, dewatering, and trenchless methods
Experience with FRP/GRP, PCCP, ductile iron, HDPE, and steel casing pipe systems
Background in CPM scheduling, budget management, change order control, and subcontractor management
Experience managing construction in active municipal environments and public right-of-way

Technical Knowledge and Tools

Proficient in Procore and Bluebeam
Proficient in Primavera P6 and/or Microsoft Project
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, Teams)
Able to read and interpret civil, structural, mechanical, and utility drawings
Familiar with municipal utility standards, specifications, and permitting

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, or a related field (equivalent field experience considered)
OSHA 30 Certification
PMP Certification or equivalent advanced project management training
Experience with design-build or CMAR project delivery
Estimating background

Salary, Benefits And Total Compensation

S.J. Louis offers a competitive compensation package for experienced senior leaders. Salary starts at $140,000 and is based on experience and qualifications.

Base Salary: Starting at $140,000 annually
Company-paid travel and lodging for all project assignments away from home
Daily per diem for overnight project assignments
Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
401(k) retirement plan
Company-paid Life Insurance
Health Savings Account (HSA)
Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
Paid Time Off (PTO)

We are looking for a senior construction professional with deep experience managing heavy civil and underground utility projects. The right candidate has a strong technical background, manages budgets and schedules with discipline, and builds solid working relationships with clients, engineers, and field crews. If you have a consistent record of delivering complex projects on time and on budget, we want to hear from you.

:

The Center for Broadening Participation in STEM (CBP-STEM) is looking for a Project Manager Research to work closely and collaboratively with Principal Investigator(s), research team, and other stakeholders to plan, direct, organize, and execute against project requirements; identify and acquire necessary resources and coordinates efforts by all parties to ensure timely delivery of project outcomes in accordance with the sponsoring source's expectations.

Plans, develops, implements, and manages a project team through complete task definitions and work requirement identification and assignments.

Key Responsibilities

Drive the Pipeline Health & Growth Committee

new_jobs.description:
Description

Application deadline: Sep 18, 2026

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services is looking for a Infrastructure Technical Program Manager to support and deploy one of the world’s largest and most complex telecommunication networks. The role is responsible for the execution of a strategic plan to improve the business processes and deployment of hyper-scaled cloud infrastructure, creation of a quality control system for North and South America (NASA), pre/post-inspections for design validation, and piloting stakeholder communication for delivery schedules. This opportunity is within the Global Connectivity Infrastructure Delivery - Fiber Deployment organization, which is responsible for project management, quality and delivery of fiber capacity for the physical network solutions that drive Amazon’s internal infrastructure and connect our services to the world.

Key job responsibilities

Reporting and Leadership: Reports to NASA GCID-FD Deployment Manager; provides regular updates to NASA and Global Senior management
Strategic Partnership: Serves as key member of North/South America GCID-FD team, driving overall Network Infrastructure strategy
Vendor Management: Manages vendor delivery timelines, measures progress, and rates performance through quality KPIs
Quality Program Development: Builds quality management program tracking defects, mitigating risks, standardizing root cause analysis, and implementing performance measures
Reporting and Stakeholder Communication: Creates standardized reporting for MFP&A; delivers regular deployment progress updates to management and stakeholders
Network Plan Tracking: Manages approved network plans with internal customers and construction vendors through to in-service delivery
Cross-Functional Program Management: Simultaneously manages multiple competing projects/programs, some at global scale
Daily Collaboration: Interfaces with engineers, technicians, vendors, and senior management
Physical Audits: Audits completed construction, reviews fiber test results, and hands off deliverables to internal customers
Risk and Escalation Management: Anticipates bottlenecks, manages risk/escalations, and balances business needs vs. technical constraints
Site Access Coordination: Coordinates access and approvals for security-regulated sites

A day in the life

This role oversees deployment of infrastructure, and iterative procedural changes. This includes travel to the field, generation of weekly reports, and updating standards and specifications for a global deployment team. This position requires onsite visits to physical locations and is not a full time remote job. Physical inspections and learning the technical standards for outside and inside fiber plant is required.

About The Team

The Global Connectivity Infrastructure Delivery - Fiber Deployment (GCID-FD) team is responsible for planning, managing, and delivering physical fiber optic network infrastructure across North and South America. The team partners with construction vendors, engineers, and internal stakeholders to deploy large-scale fiber networks on time and to the highest quality standards. Through rigorous vendor management, quality control programs, and cross-functional collaboration, GCID-FD ensures network infrastructure moves from approved plans to in-service delivery. The team drives network strategy, manages risk, and coordinates complex deployments across security-regulated sites to support global connectivity goals.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of technical infrastructure management experience
Knowledge of best practices and emerging technologies, related to infrastructure (i.e. network, data center, hardware, software)
Experience with varying scenarios of infrastructure builds
You must have 3+ years experience managing third-party construction or infrastructure vendors, including tracking delivery timelines, measuring performance through KPIs, and implementing corrective actions when quality standards.
You must have 3+ years experience auditing completed construction, reviewing fiber test results or similar deliverables, and coordinating site access in security-regulated environments.
You must have 3+ years experience proactively identifying deployment bottlenecks, managing escalations, and balancing business needs against technical constraints to keep projects on track.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a network planning, network construction/implementation, or commercial implementation role at an ISP, telecoms operator, or Hyperscaler

Description

Company Overview

PCS Retirement, LLC, a subsidiary of FSG Parent L.P., is one of the nation's largest independent and conflict-free retirement solution providers in the industry. PCS provides recordkeeping services to 19,000 plans and 850,000 eligible participants representing more than $26 billion in assets under administration. PCS' comprehensive retirement solutions platform includes business development tools for financial advisors, a data-driven recordkeeping technology that supports all types of retirement plans [401(k), 403(b), 457, Cash Balance, Defined Benefit, Non-Qualified], individual retirement accounts (including payroll deduction IRAs), and health savings accounts.

At PCS Retirement, we cultivate an environment built on trust, where every team member is empowered to take ownership and contribute to our shared vision. Through collaborative teamwork we foster growth, both personally and professionally, ensuring that together we exceed expectations and achieve remarkable success.

To learn more, visit https://www.pcsretirement.com/

Job Summary

The project manager position is responsible for leading/managing various Product, Technology and Lean Management related projects for a fast-growing company in the 401k and retirement services sector. The position requires working with Product Owners, IT resources, business stakeholders and executive leadership to scope projects, develop and implement project plans while taking ownership of delivering projects on time and on budget.

This role is responsible for leading the project team members throughout the lifecycle of a project, including developing, implementing, and executing planning efforts while ensuring the appropriate PM artifacts such as Charter, Plan, Update, ROI Summary, Communication & Closing/Retro documents are leveraged within established best practices.

Job Responsibilities

Manages a portfolio of projects including high exposure & complex technology focused initiatives that will drive significant return across the firm.
Leads project teams in coordination activities, including facilitation of project kickoff meetings, weekly project status meetings, work break down and status tracking, project / program reporting and project closure activities.
Ensures that project team tasks are appropriately allocated to the team members best equipped to complete them and ensure appropriately reallocation of tasks across the team to ensure projects are delivered on time.
Takes ownership in delivering projects on time, escalating issues as identified while working swiftly to remove barriers that present risks to the project.
Resolves project team issues quickly and makes effective decisions, in collaboration with PCS management, to keep team members productive on an ongoing basis.
Establishes project team execution standards and meeting cadences, including the standard usage of project management tool usage in a manner consistent with program management guidelines.
Partners closely with Product Owners and members of IT resources to manage technology focused projects.
Performing quality control on the project throughout development to maintain the standards expected.
Effectively manages new project team demand, including facilitating and managing new work (intake) requests and change controls.
Works with the project team, as well as internal and external stakeholders, to influence and drive decision making for key decisions impacting the project team’s scope, costs, resources and schedules.
Contributes to the advancement and improvement of project management practices and tools across the organization. Coaches team members, business partners and stakeholders on project management best practices.
Leads ROI calculation discussions, and documents forecasted returns.
Effectively communicates with senior leadership to ensure the projects are aligned with their goals

Bachelor's degree in business administration, management information systems, computer science, or related field highly desired.
5+ years of expert project management experience in financial services.
Project Management certifications, including PMP, CSM and/or SAFE Agilist, highly desired.
Understanding of both agile and waterfall methodologies, experience leading agile scrum teams in a remote environment, preferably with at least 2 years of experience being a SCRUM master.
Experience managing cross-functional remote project teams of various sizes (smaller vs larger teams) and understanding of the appropriate project management techniques dependent on team size.
Proven experience with business and technical analysis, business process modeling/mapping.
Excellent judgment, decision making skills, and the ability to work under continual deadline pressure.
Demonstrated ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment and collaborating across geographically distributed remote teams.
Excellent listening, written and verbal communications / presentation skills, and experience presenting to senior executives, decision makers, and external stakeholders.
Ability to work independently with minimal direction and comfortable working through ambiguity.
Excellent analytical and creative problem-solving skills.
Proficient with project management tools (Jira, Confluence, and Salesforce), and office productivity tools (MS Office: Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook).

new_jobs.title: Hardware Production Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
About Us

Zeitview is the leading intelligent aerial imaging company for high-value infrastructure, providing businesses with actionable, real-time insights to recover revenue, reduce risk and improve build quality. We serve customers in the solar, wind, insurance, construction, real estate, and critical infrastructure industries. Trusted by the largest enterprises in the world, Zeitview is active in over 70 countries. Our mission is to accelerate the global transition to renewable energy and sustainable infrastructure through advanced inspection solutions. Take a look at our latest achievements here!

About The Role

We are seeking a Hardware Production Program Manager to own the end-to-end production planning, qualification, and lifecycle of our cutting-edge aerial sensors and robotic drone payloads.

In this role, you will bridge the gap between complex hardware design and flawless operational execution. You will run the programs behind New Product Introduction (NPI), repeat production builds, and sustain engineering support for our existing fleet - driving schedules, procurement, and cross-team coordination. If you are a natural problem solver who thrives in a fast-paced robotics environment and loves turning complex engineering prototypes into reliable, scalable products, we want to hear from you.

Responsibilities

Production Program Management & NPI
:

Own the hardware build ecosystem: Create and manage comprehensive NPI and repeat build timelines, ensuring procurement, staffing, tooling, and documentation are set up for success.
Balance the fleet: Align closely with Operations to understand hardware demand and field repair needs. Partner with the technicians and their functional leads to sequence work across new builds, repairs, and fleet movements.
Procurement ownership: Manage procurement pipelines and BOMs, and execute procurement with vendors for a majority of sourced components.
Production leadership: Hire and develop staffing required to meet production and sustainment volumes. Develop and leverage external vendors for production when commercially reasonable.
Schedule and risk ownership: Maintain the single source of truth for build status, dependencies, and risk. Escalate early and clearly when timelines are threatened.

Sustaining Engineering & Cross-Functional Coordination

Technical conduit: Act as the primary technical bridge across engineering and operations teams to accelerate debugging and issue resolution.
Field support: Coordinate troubleshooting of complex issues occurring in the field; ensure clear ownership is assigned and root-cause resolutions are documented.
Process scaling: Scope and implement critical process improvements for part tracking, unit history, and issue tracking as our hardware scales.
System Performance Management: Track issues across hardware fleet under support to identify common issues and develop solutions to implement in the field to reduce excessive costs and improve system performance.
Blocker mitigation: Anticipate production or field blockers early and implement creative, agile engineering solutions to keep timelines on track.

Qualifications
:.

Experience: 5+ years in engineering, product development, hardware program management, or hardware manufacturing, with a strong preference for complex robotic, aerospace, or drone platforms.
Program leadership: Proven track record driving hardware programs to completion through influence rather than direct authority - coordinating technicians, engineers, and vendors toward a shared schedule.
Technical breadth: A deep understanding of electro-mechanical assemblies, aerial sensors, and payload integration, allowing you to assess field issues and dive deep into root-cause analysis when required.
Execution & agility: The ability to ruthlessly prioritize competing demands, manage tight timelines with many moving pieces, and creatively fill operational gaps.
Process-driven mindset: Proven track record of developing tools, documentation (SOPs), or processes to improve build efficiency and consistency.
Communication: Exceptional, concise communication skills with the ability to translate highly technical issues into clear updates for cross-functional stakeholders.
Ability to travel: Support a distributed engineering team and worldwide operations. Travel up to 10% of time may be required.
AI proficiency: A track record of leveraging AI to solve operational challenges, balanced with the discernment to recognize its limitations. You proactively deploy your own technical toolkit to drive results.

What Would Make You Stand Out

Experience with PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) and ERP systems for tracking hardware changes and inventory.
Experience with manufacturing testers (electrical, mechanical, reliability) to qualify built systems or subassemblies.
Experience managing contract manufacturers or outsourced build partners.

What’s Included

Feel great about your work as you join a leading mission-driven intelligent aerial imaging company - our goal is to accelerate the global transition to renewable energy and sustainable infrastructure, and you personally will play a large part in making this happen!
Hybrid work setting: 2 days/week in our Mountain View office (days are flexible), and other days are 100% remote
Competitive salary, bonus and eligibility for stock options
Your choice of multiple medical insurance plans, including options with an HSA and 100% coverage of the premium for yourself and your dependents
100% paid dental and vision insurance
Unlimited PTO: We mean it when we say we prioritize work-life balance and mental health
Autonomy and upward mobility
Diverse, equitable, and inclusive culture: a place where your voice matters

This role has a base salary range of $110,000 - $120,000 USD, plus a target annual bonus and eligibility for stock options. Actual compensation may vary based on experience, skills, and location within the USA.

new_jobs.title: Senior Strategic Implementation Manager
new_jobs.description:
Kestra Financial is a wealth management platform dedicated to empowering independent financial professionals—including traditional and hybrid RIAs—to grow their businesses and deliver exceptional client service. We combine advanced business management technology with personalized consulting to provide unmatched scale, efficiency, and support. Our advisor-focused culture is built on innovation and advocacy, enabling advisors to offer comprehensive securities and investment advisory solutions to their clients

Lead with Purpose. Partner with Impact

Kestra Financial, a leading provider of wealth management platforms, technology solutions, and investment products empowering independent financial advisors and RIAs nationwide, is seeking a Senior Strategic Implementation Manager.

This role serves as a pivotal execution leader accountable for the disciplined delivery of Kestra Wealth Management’s highest-priority strategic initiatives in investment products and platform capabilities. You will drive the successful launch of new investment products and manage end-to-end launch campaigns while coordinating complex cross-functional projects spanning technology, compliance, business development, and operations.

By implementing and championing agile, Scrum-like cadences and robust portfolio governance practices, you will build transparency, predictability, and accountability across initiatives. Your leadership will ensure that strategic intent translates into measurable business outcomes—including accelerated advisor adoption, revenue contribution from new products, enhanced platform capabilities, and operational excellence.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role for a collaborative leader who thrives at the intersection of strategy, execution, and cross-functional influence in a dynamic, growth-oriented wealth management environment.

What You’ll Do:

Own the end-to-end governance and planning that results in successful delivery of priority investment product launches (e.g., alternative investment solutions, insurance products, or curated offerings) and strategic platform implementation initiatives (new advisory revenue vertical, investment program redesign, etc) from concept through post-launch optimization and benefits realization.
Lead the coordination and execution of comprehensive launch campaigns, aligning go-to-market activities including sales enablement, marketing communications, advisor training and onboarding programs, distribution strategy, and adoption tracking to drive rapid uptake and sustained engagement.
Establish and maintain a prioritized portfolio of strategic initiatives for Investment Platforms & Products; drive rigorous sequencing, capacity alignment, funding discipline, and proactive trade-off decisions (scope, timeline, resources, investment) aligned to Kestra’s business objectives and growth priorities.
Partner with Product Management to translate product strategy and roadmap into executable implementation plans with clear milestones, dependencies, and success criteria.
Support Wealth Management platform and product leads by facilitating high-performing cross-functional project teams and workstreams involving:
Technology: Platform development, data integrations (including MDM/medallion architectures), APIs, advisor portals/tools, and infrastructure enhancements.
Compliance & Legal: Product due diligence, regulatory reviews/approvals, disclosures, risk assessments, and ongoing product governance to ensure adherence to SEC, FINRA, fiduciary, and other requirements.
Business: Commercialization strategy, RIA/advisor engagement and feedback loops, distribution channel readiness, pricing/packaging, and P&L impact modeling.
Operations & Finance: Operational readiness, process design, financial tracking, and benefits measurement.
Map and manage complex dependencies, risks, and interdependencies across teams; proactively identify and remove blockers while fostering alignment and shared ownership in a matrixed environment.
Ensure every initiative incorporates appropriate compliance guardrails, risk controls, audit readiness, and change management from the start.
Design, implement, and continuously mature agile delivery operating models tailored to regulated investment product and platform initiatives. This includes establishing Scrum-like cadences (sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, retrospectives), Kanban for workflow transparency and flow optimization, and scaled frameworks (e.g., program-level planning or release management) for larger or interdependent efforts.
Stand up consistent governance rhythms and forums, including steering committees, launch readiness reviews/tollgates, dependency management sessions, risk reviews, and clear escalation paths to executive leadership.
Drive adoption of modern agile/project tools (Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or equivalent) and best practices to improve delivery velocity, predictability, collaboration, and quality across technology and business teams.
Champion a shift toward iterative, outcome-focused delivery—balancing the need for structure and compliance in product launches with the speed and adaptability required in a competitive wealth tech landscape.
Build and operate a portfolio “control tower” capability: deliver timely, credible, decision-oriented reporting and dashboards on initiative status, milestones, risks/issues, dependencies, financial performance (budget vs. plan, ROI tracking), and leading indicators of business impact.
Define, track, and report on key business outcome metrics tied to each strategic initiative (e.g., new product net flows/AUM/revenue contribution, advisor adoption and usage rates, client/advisor satisfaction or NPS impact, reduction in time-to-market or launch cycle time, compliance adherence, platform feature utilization and engagement).
Proactively surface execution risks, capacity constraints, and recommended trade-offs to senior leadership; lead structured issue resolution, corrective action planning, and recovery efforts to protect delivery commitments and protect/enhance business results.
Prepare and present high-quality materials for executive leadership, steering committees, and governance forums; represent the delivery health and outlook of the Investment Platforms & Products portfolio with clarity and fact-based insights.
Instill a culture of genuine accountability—where teams own and are measured on the delivery of agreed business outcomes and value realization, not merely activity completion or milestone hitting.

What You Bring: 

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or Software Engineering.
2+ years experience in technical product management in an Agile environment.
5+ years of experience in wealth management, investment operations, or trading
3-5+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic program/portfolio management, product implementation, launch execution, or enterprise transformation roles within wealth management, RIA platforms, investment product development, fintech, asset/wealth platforms, or similarly complex, regulated financial services environments.
Demonstrated success leading multiple end-to-end launches of investment products or major platform capabilities, including coordination across technology builds, compliance/regulatory approvals, and go-to-market execution
Direct experience with alternatives/private markets access, model portfolios, structured solutions, or advisor-facing technology platforms within a broker dealer organization is strongly preferred.
Track record of successfully implementing or significantly maturing agile delivery practices (Scrum, Kanban, SAFe, hybrid, or tailored approaches) in product development or regulated contexts, with quantifiable improvements in predictability, velocity, and time-to-value.

Certifications and Licenses:

Series 7 , 63 or 66 required within 2 years.
Series 65 preferred

Internal applicants must be in good standing and have a minimum of 1 year of service with Kestra. Internal applicants must also have a minimum of 1 year service in current role unless approved by EVP.

Benefits to support you:

Competitive pay and benefits with a large employer (over 1600 employees nationwide)
401(k), health insurance, and a competitive benefits package
Work in a supportive, collaborative environment committed to professional excellence
Help clients navigate meaningful financial decisions with confidence
Opportunities for training, development, and long-term growth within the firm
Tuition reimbursement for qualified expenses

Our Mission is Powering Financial Independence, enabling the growth and success of investing clients and the advisors who serve them. We do that by living our values: Serve, Make it Happen, and One team.

new_jobs.title: Healing to Advocacy Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Essie Justice Group (Essie) is building grassroots power to dismantle the US incarceration system, the most egregious creator of racial and gender injustice of our time. We are a loving and powerful community of women with incarcerated loved ones. Our community includes cisgender women, transgender women, formerly incarcerated women, gender expansive people, elders, and young people.

After twelve years of building an active membership across California and beyond, Essie is deepening its base-building and leadership development strategies with the 1 in 4 women with incarcerated loved ones to propel bold decarceration agendas across the nation. We seek to transform the criminal legal system and create a Black feminist future rooted in care, equity, community safety, and liberation.

The ideal candidate understands and believes passionately in people power and is deeply interested in the leadership development of the people most impacted by the systems we seek to change. The Healing to Advocacy Program Manager is a crucial leader within our organization, charged with managing staff and the day-to-day operations of Essie’s signature organizing program. The ideal candidate is a master project manager and executor who thoroughly enjoys implementing large and growing programs. The ideal candidate will also have an important role in recommending changes to the Healing to Advocacy Program and leading in implementing those changes. What the person in this role loves to do is make sure things happen and happen well. The ideal candidate can thoughtfully create work plans; delegate and support others in program implementation; bring out the best in staff, contractors, and members through strong management and people skills; and drive themselves and the staff they supervise towards goals.

Core Responsibilities

Manage Essie’s Healing To Advocacy Organizing Program

Management: Directly Manage 1-2 staff members and run the day-to-day operations of the Healing to Advocacy Program. Key functions include:
Logistics: Create a top-notch logistics plan to reduce barriers to participation. Solve complex logistical problems related to the different parts of the program and in response to the needs of members.
Childcare Program: Manage and co-design the EssieKids! Program, ensuring childcare needs are reasonably met within the Healing to Advocacy Program.
Contractor & Relationship Management: Manage contractors, including childcare providers, guest trainers, and other specialists. Hold external relationships necessary to run the overall program successfully.
Member Recruitment & Cohort Filling: Coordinate and oversee the implementation of a member recruitment strategy. Member recruitment involves thousands of nomination letters from incarcerated people, coordinating a nominations committee to make phone calls to the nominees, and filling dozens of member cohorts statewide.
Recruit and Manage Member Facilitators: Identify, onboard, and support member facilitators who co-lead program sessions and activities, ensuring they are trained and prepared to engage cohorts effectively.
Cohort Launch: Launch cohorts in 15-20 different locations across the state.
Cohort Graduations: Coordinate a team of staff and members to ensure that 2-4 Healing to Advocacy Graduation events occur per year that graduate multiple cohorts each and officially welcome cohort participants into Essie’s advocacy body and membership.
Evaluation: Manage data and administration goals during all parts of the program.

Member Training & Support

Coordinate the multi-day agenda and facilitate the Essie Facilitator Training Retreats to prepare Essie members to run cohorts in their areas.
Respond in a culture and values-aligned manner to needs, concerns, and recommendations from Healing to Advocacy Facilitators and program participants.
Track and share the leadership development outcomes with the Directors’ Team through strategic data collection, presentation of information, and uplifting actionable recommendations.

Team Leadership

Ensure the program is meeting its stated goals as set by the and the collaboratively created Operational Plan;co-designing and implementing a program evaluation system.
Proactively provide input on programmatic improvements.
Manage and train staff and contractors who are carrying out core functions of the Healing to Advocacy Program (i.e. childcare, staff organizers, trainers, graphic designers) to achieve set organizational goals together.
Oversee member retention, recruitment, evaluation, and data management systems design related to the program.

Who We’re Looking For

Ideal Qualifications

3-5 years of experience in complex program implementation, preferably in community organizing or direct services contexts.
Detail-oriented project manager with experience managing multiple, complex projects at once.
Understands and demonstrates knowledge of best practices in recruitment, retention, and Black feminist culture-setting.
Excellent prioritization skills (i.e. understands the difference between what’s important, urgent, and what is neither).
Advanced experience in facilitating retreats, workshops, and/or political education trainings.
Experience supervising people in a way that acknowledges differentials in privilege and power, recognizes their gifts, encourages their confidence, supports their growth, and holds them accountable to standards and achieving collective goals.
Effective writing, editing, and verbal communication skills.
Track record as a collaborative leader.

Qualities

Program manager extraordinaire. You believe in the power of an excellently designed and run program as a key avenue for social and personal change. You build air-tight plans, through your skill as an “if, then” thinker, mitigating risks of a plan failing by imagining and preparing for various scenarios, smart prioritization, and advance problem-solving. If things go wrong or when faced with an unforeseen complexity you draw on your professional experience and flexibility to come up with possibilities and motivate others.
You’re very into root causes. You think about programmatic challenges from a big picture lens, wondering if what you observe is a symptom of a broader problem, and identifying possible patterns and system-based solutions to address it.
Discernment and honesty we can trust. You are a thoughtful team member who acts in alignment with your integrity and are unfailingly trustworthy.
Committed to evolution. You are committed to continuously deepening and evolving your own understanding of systems of oppression through study, openness, and humility. And, you easily recognize your own relationship to privilege and power, examining and shifting your behaviors as appropriate.
Uplifting and additive. You see mistakes as opportunities for growth; problems as catalysts for solutions, and inspire others along difficult journeys. You carry a positive approach, can-do attitude, a sense of humor, and authentic kindness wherever you go. You can lead from an authentic and calm place to help others feel confident, assured and hopeful that possibilities exist in the face of challenge or uncertainty.

The Position

The Healing to Advocacy Program Manager is a full-time, salaried, exempt position. This position leads the Healing to Advocacy Program and reports to the Associate Director of Strategy & Organizational Impact. The salary for this position is between $90,000 - $95,000 depending on experience, with full medical, dental, and vision benefits, optional 401(k), a substantial vacation package, and a monthly personal wellness stipend. The position can be based at either of Essie’s offices in Los Angeles or Oakland, California.

To Apply

Please address a personal, specific, and thoughtful cover letter to the “Essie Hiring Committee” and submit along with a resume through our hiring portal (https://essiejusticegroup.bamboohr.com/jobs). Your resume tells us what you can do; your cover letter should tell us who you are and why you want to work with Essie.

Essie Justice Group provides equal employment and advancement opportunities to all staff members. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and skills. Essie does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, immigration status, socioeconomic status, ancestry, age, size, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, familial status, veteran status, disability, AIDS/HIV status, medical condition, prior conviction, arrest history, traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Essie values and specifically seeks applicants who are people with incarcerated loved ones; formerly incarcerated people; people of color; women; queer, transgender, gender expansive, and gender fluid people.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, performance assessment, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

About Essie Justice Group

Essie Justice Group is a non profit organization of women with incarcerated loved ones taking on the rampant injustices created by mass incarceration. Our award-winning Healing to Advocacy Model brings women together to heal, build collective power, and drive social change. Essie is

Learn more at www.essiejusticegroup.org.
